justice: The corridor allocates substantial space to motor traffic with multiple wide vehicle lanes, while pedestrian space is only visible at the edges behind hedges and a fence, suggesting an uneven distribution of street space for all users.

A bus stop shelter is visible on the left, which supports broader access to public transport, but no visible marked crossing connects both sides of the road to that stop, limiting fair access across the corridor.

The sidewalks appear physically separated from traffic by green medians and hedges, which helps basic accessibility, but no curb ramps, tactile paving, or barrier-free crossing details are visible in the image.

The right-side white fence and continuous hedge create a protected edge for pedestrians, yet they may also constrain direct access points if crossings are infrequent, reducing accessibility for users not traveling by car.
Cycling provision is not visible: there is no bike lane marking, cycle track, or bicycle signal shown, so spatial resources appear less equitably distributed for non-motorized users.
safety: The roadway has clear lane markings and a landscaped median, which organize vehicle movement and reduce head-on conflict risk for all road users.

Street lighting poles are visible along the corridor, supporting nighttime traffic safety, although the image does not show pavement-level lighting quality for pedestrians.
livability: The street is lined with mature trees and continuous greenery on both sides and in the median, creating a pleasant and healthier everyday environment.

The scene appears clean, orderly, and well maintained, with trimmed hedges, intact pavement markings, and healthy tree canopy contributing positively to livability.
sustainability: Extensive tree canopy and planted medians provide significant green infrastructure, which supports shade, cooling, and ecological value.
The visible bus stop and bus in traffic indicate that the corridor supports public transport, which is more sustainable than car-only travel.

The broad asphalt carriageway still prioritizes motor vehicle movement, so sustainability benefits from transit and greenery are partly offset by car-oriented design.
aesthetics: The avenue of mature trees on both sides creates a strong, coherent visual identity and a high-quality green streetscape.
Trimmed hedges in the median and roadside strips give the corridor a neat, well-maintained appearance.

comfort: Dense tree canopy along both sides provides substantial shade for sidewalks and roadside areas, supporting good thermal comfort in warm weather.
